title: Adaptive exposure controller and sequential A/B checks for model rollouts
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a first-class A/B testing framework for model variants focused on safe exposure, sequential statistical checks, and automated rollback. This ticket scopes an adaptive exposure controller (fractional traffic scheduler), a library of sequential hypothesis tests tuned for low-latency streams, and integration points with the Console for experiment setup and metrics-driven rollback policies. The feature must work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and support shadow traffic and canary-style phased rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Console can create an experiment with: target model versions, control/variant assignment, initial exposure fraction, escalation policy, and rollback thresholds
Adaptive exposure controller increases exposure automatically when key metrics pass sequential checks and throttles or rolls back when regressions are detected
Support for shadow traffic: duplicates of live traffic can be sent to variants without user impact and included in offline evaluation streams
Statistical library implements sequential tests (e.g., alpha-spending, SPRT, and Bayesian sequential models) with configurable confidence and minimum sample constraints
Experiments produce traceable artifacts: start/end timestamps, per-window metric deltas, p-values/Bayes factors, and a final experiment decision accessible via API and Console
Automatic rollback triggers an orchestrated fallback to the previous pinned model, emits an incident event, and records a postmortem checklist entry
End-to-end tests validate exposure ramping, metric gating, and rollback in Hosted and Dedicated local integration environments
tasks: Spec: write PRD with API contract for experiment creation, exposure policy grammar, and rollback actions
Design: Console UX for experiment wizard and real-time status panel (coord with design team)
Engineering: implement exposure controller service with rate-limited increments and cooldown windows
Engineering: implement sequential statistical checks as a shared library (C++/Rust runtime bindings + Python SDK)
Engineering: wire metrics ingestion (per-request labels) into experiment windows and incorporate latency, error-rate, and quality evals
QA: create synthetic traffic harness to validate canary ramps, shadowing, and rollback choreography
Docs: doc the experiment API, recommended metric sets, and example runbooks for rollouts and incidents
notes: Design decision: prefer sequential testing to fixed-window A/B because of streaming nature and desire for faster decisions with controlled false positive rate. Trade-offs: more conservative alpha-spending reduces rollout speed; aggressive spending speeds adoption but increases risk. Initial implementation will support a small set of common metrics (latency P95, token cost delta, failure rate, and a model-quality score) with an extension point for custom metrics. We will default to canary-style 1%, 5%, 20% ramps for quick experiments and allow custom schedules. Security review flagged KMS access for audit logs in Private deployments; ENG-3345 will address KMS integration.
